title: Returning goods
text:
RETURNS POLICY
If you are not satisfied with your purchase, you may return it within 28 days for a full refund, as long as it is unused and in its original packaging. Please bring your receipt; without one, we can offer an exchange or store credit only. Sale items can be returned for store credit but not for a refund. Items bought online can be returned to any of our shops or sent back by post using the free returns label included with your order. Refunds are made to the original method of payment and may take up to five working days to appear. Faulty goods may be returned at any time within one year.

title: Train replacement buses
text:
ENGINEERING WORK: 14-16 OCTOBER
No trains will run between Ashby and Calder on these dates. Replacement buses will leave from the bus stop outside the station's main entrance every 20 minutes. title: Community garden: how to join
text: Greenfield Community Garden has 40 plots available for local residents. Plots cost £25 a year, and water and basic tools are provided free of charge. New members must attend a short induction session, held on the first Saturday of each month. Plot holders are expected to keep their plot tidy and to grow something on at least three quarters of it. If a plot is neglected for more than two months, it may be offered to someone on the waiting list. Bonfires are not permitted. Members can use the shared composting area, and we hold a produce swap every Sunday in the summer.

title: Customer service adviser
text: Harbour Energy is looking for customer service advisers to join our team in Lexton. You will answer customer calls and online messages about bills, meter readings and new accounts. No previous experience is required, as full training is given during your first four weeks, but you must have good communication skills and be comfortable using computers. The role is full-time, 37.5 hours a week, on a rota that includes one Saturday in every four. After six months, advisers may apply to work from home for up to two days a week. The starting salary is £24,000, rising after successful completion of training. Benefits include 25 days' annual leave, a pension scheme and free parking. To apply, send your CV and a short covering letter to recruitment@harbourenergy.example by 30 November.

title: Sickness absence procedure
text: If you are unable to come to work because of illness, you must telephone your line manager before 9.30 am on the first day of absence. A text message or email is not acceptable unless you are unable to speak. You should explain the nature of your illness and when you expect to return. For absences of up to seven calendar days, you will need to complete a self-certification form when you return. For longer absences, a fit note from a doctor is required. On your return after any absence of more than three days, your manager will hold a short return-to-work meeting with you to check that you are well enough to carry out your duties and to discuss any support you need. Repeated short absences may lead to a formal review.

title: Fire safety training
text: All staff must complete fire safety training once a year. The training consists of a 30-minute online course followed by a practical session with the building's fire warden. The online course can be completed at any time, but must be finished before you attend the practical session. Practical sessions take place on the second Tuesday of every month in Meeting Room 3. During the session you will learn how to use the different types of fire extinguisher and walk through the evacuation route from your work area. Staff who work night shifts can arrange an individual session by contacting the facilities team. Your manager will receive a report showing who has not completed the training.

title: Working from home policy
text: Employees who have completed their probation period may request to work from home for up to two days a week. Requests should be made in writing to your manager, who will respond within ten working days. Approval depends on the needs of your team, and your manager may ask you to come into the office on particular days for meetings. title: Writing a good covering letter
text: A covering letter introduces you to an employer and explains why you are applying. Keep it to one page. Begin by stating which job you are applying for and where you saw it advertised. In the main part, choose two or three of your strongest skills or experiences and show how they match the requirements in the job description, giving a specific example for each. Avoid simply repeating your CV. Employers also want to know why you are interested in their organisation in particular, so do some research beforehand. End by saying that you would welcome the chance of an interview. Always check spelling carefully, and address the letter to a named person if possible rather than 'Dear Sir or Madam'.
